## TL;DR

Close-out and handoff on remote validators (bee, thinkpad, mini) kept failing the same handful of timing-shaped tests while unrelated tasks were green. The failures were real environmental coupling in the tests, not regressions in the branches under review. This change removes those couplings: injected pressure probes no longer blend with live CPU-idle sampling, review chat polls use the shared 60s spawn helpers, engineer resource-limit tests drain capacity queues before asserting spawn records, and host-lock fixtures synchronize with gate files and portable stale mtimes instead of fixed sleeps or widened timeouts. Production lock and pressure behaviour is unchanged.

## Work and rationale

The task listed nine failing tests across four files. Investigation followed `docs/debugging-check-failures.md` and prior incidents (#1101 host-lock queue, #1118 holder/waiter sync, #0891 pressure guard in agent tests).

**Pressure guard.** `waitForPressureRelief` loops call `pressureSnapshot(config, probe)`. Even with a two-step fake probe (pressure then relief), the snapshot always appended `sampleCpuIdlePercent()`. On a loaded validator the second poll’s CPU delta often read below `minIdleCpuPercent`, so relief never arrived and ThinkPad close-out failed the relief test (also seen on #1075/#1098). The fix omits live CPU sampling whenever an explicit probe is supplied, exports `resetCpuIdleSampling()` for tests, and allows sub-500ms polling when a probe is injected (the 500ms floor remains for real-machine waits). A regression test asserts relief snapshots stay null while a live CPU sample would read busy.

**Agent review.** The reviewer-chat test and several helpers used private 10s async polls while `tests/helpers.ts` standardized on 60s for process-spawning E2E. Under remote suite load the second `opencode` spawn for chat continuation could exceed 10s without being broken. Poll ceilings and intervals now reuse `WAIT_FOR_TIMEOUT_MS` and `WAIT_FOR_POLL_MS`.

**Agent drivers.** `AgentRunner.start()` may return `{ ok: true, queued: true }` when waiting for a concurrent-agent slot. The resource-limits test only asserted `ok` and waited for the fakebin log; a queued start on a busy host presented as a spawn timeout. The test now waits for `isQueued` to clear before reading spawn env.

**Remote host pool.** For #1101’s deferred-queue test, a 200ms sleep before the lock shell was not a synchronization primitive: under scheduler delay the shell could scan an empty queue and acquire. The parent now drops a `queue-ready` file only after dead and live wait entries exist. For the orphan stale-break test, `touch -t` alone failed on some validators (#1122); the test now uses `utimesSync`, a GNU/BSD touch fallback, and a preflight mtime assertion, with `waitSecs` tightened to 15s because the point is breaking the orphan on the first stale sweep—not surviving a 30s wall clock. The holder/waiter test already used HOLDER_STARTED sync (#1118); no production shell change was required beyond #1101’s queue scan behaviour already on main.

## Approaches tried

- Ran the named tests in isolation, concurrently, and in repeated batches (50× for pressure relief, 20× for the three lock cases, 25× for engineer resource limits) on this workstation; all green after fixes.
- Confirmed the pressure-guard failure mode by reading `pressureSnapshot` and cross-checking ThinkPad handoff logs from #1098.
- Did not raise vitest `testTimeout` for the orphan case beyond restoring 30s after shortening the lock wait budget.

## Challenges and blockers

- **50× under artificial load on every test on remote runners** (bee and thinkpad) is an acceptance item that requires the human validation fleet; this session verified locally under concurrent vitest and repeated runs, not on bee/thinkpad hardware.
- The orphan stress loop with a background `yes` load generator was stopped by the environment time limit before printing a final count; sequential 20× batches of the lock trio completed with zero failures.

## Key learnings

- **Injected probes must own the whole snapshot.** Any live host signal (CPU idle, paging activity) mixed into a fake memory probe recreates “flake on loaded validator, pass in isolation.”
- **Do not duplicate wait budgets.** A 10s local poll inside a file that imports 60s helpers will fail first under load and waste close-out time.
- **`ok: true` ≠ spawned.** Queue metadata from `spawnOrQueue` needs the same polling discipline as subprocess logs.
- **Shell tests need explicit gates, not sleeps.** File markers (`queue-ready`, `HOLDER_STARTED`) tie correctness to fixture state, not machine speed.
